1.title: What Is a Clos? The Key Difference from Grand Cru
1.html:
In Alsace, a "Clos" means a separate single plot with clear boundaries (often walled), owned or controlled exclusively by a single estate. A Clos is not part of the official AOC classification — it may lie within a Grand Cru (such as Clos Saint-Urbain within Rangen) or stand entirely outside the Grand Cru system.

What makes a Clos distinctive: some Clos harvest, press and vinify several varieties together — different from Edelzwicker (a blend of finished wines) or Gentil (vinified separately and then blended), this is a tradition closer to a "field blend", and the reason a Clos style stands apart.
2.title: A Tour of Famous Alsace Clos (Part 1)
2.items.0.label: Clos Sainte Hune (Hunawihr, 1.67 ha)
2.items.0.desc: 100% Riesling, exclusively owned by the F.E. Trimbach estate, in the mid-slope of the Rosacker Grand Cru. One of the most esteemed Rieslings in Alsace and the world, regarded as the peak representative of Alsace Riesling.
2.items.1.label: Clos Windsbuhl (Hunawihr)
2.items.1.desc: A separate plot run by the Zind-Humbrecht estate, located in Turckheim, with a calcareous (chalk and clay) steep slope terroir, famous for concentration and minerality.
2.items.2.label: Clos Saint-Urbain (Thann, within Rangen)
2.items.2.desc: Owned by the Zind-Humbrecht estate, a separate plot inside the Rangen Grand Cru, with Gewurztraminer / Riesling / Pinot Gris, showing the unique imprint of volcanic geology.
2.items.3.label: Clos du Zahnacker (Ribeauvillé)
2.items.3.desc: Owned by the Ribeauvillé cooperative, with the three varieties each making up 1/3: Gewurztraminer, Pinot Gris and Riesling — the three varieties are harvested, pressed and vinified together, completely different from Edelzwicker (a blend of finished wines).
3.title: A Tour of Famous Alsace Clos (Part 2)
3.items.0.label: Clos des Capucins (Kientzheim)
3.items.0.desc: Exclusively owned by Domaine Weinbach (the Théo-Faller family), with several wines of Pinot Gris, Gewurztraminer and Riesling, one of the signature plots of Alsace's most famous family estates.
3.items.1.label: Clos Saint Landelin (Rouffach)
3.items.1.desc: Owned by the René Muré estate, planted with Muscat / Pinot Gris / Riesling / Gewurztraminer, a well-known separate plot within the Vorbourg Grand Cru.
3.items.2.label: Clos de Meywihr (Ammerschwihr)
3.items.2.desc: Owned by Roger Klein, within the Kaefferkopf area, only 10 ares 60 centiares — the smallest Clos in all Alsace!
3.items.3.label: Clos Rebgarten (Andlau)
3.items.3.desc: Owned by Domaine F. Gresser / Marc Kreydenweiss, 100% Muscat — a rare single-variety Muscat Clos, showing the refined expression of this rare variety.
4.question: How does the "several varieties harvested and pressed together" practice of a Clos like Clos du Zahnacker fundamentally differ from an Edelzwicker blend?
4.options.0: The two are exactly the same, just with different names
4.options.1: Zahnacker is harvested, pressed and vinified with several varieties together (like a field blend); Edelzwicker is mostly a blend of finished wines (each variety vinified separately and then mixed)
4.options.2: Edelzwicker can use only a single variety
4.options.3: Zahnacker can only be used for Grand Cru plots
4.explanation: The three varieties of Clos du Zahnacker (Gewurztraminer, Pinot Gris, Riesling) are harvested, pressed and fermented together, a tradition closer to a "field blend"; Edelzwicker is mostly made by mixing finished wines (or separately fermented liquids) of each variety. The two differ fundamentally in winemaking logic, and so produce different flavour complexity.
